items.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.summary_1line: Serving web queries at scale with multi-agent systems requires jointly configuring large language models, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills. However, the resulting configuration space g...
items.editor_note: Moves the technique from training a model to choosing multi-agent serving configurations.

editorial.tldr: Papers from Oct 14 onward apply on-policy distillation (training a student on its own sampled trajectories, scored by a teacher) to translation, long-horizon coding agents, and the question of when the student should follow the teacher.
editorial.whats_new: Oct 26: EvoRouter, an arXiv paper, uses insight-guided on-policy distillation to pick models, agent counts and skills for multi-agent web-query serving at lower cost.
editorial.why_it_matters: On-policy distillation is moving from model post-training into serving decisions such as multi-agent routing, so cost-focused teams can test it on configuration choices, not only on small models.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you distill small models or tune multi-agent configs, run an on-policy versus SFT comparison on your own trajectories and query mix before adopting either; none of these papers has independent replication yet.

beats.headline: Qwen-MT-Lumen applies on-policy training to WMT 2026 translation
OPRD distills constraint reminders into long-horizon coding agents
Advantage-based method decides when to follow the teacher
EvoRouter applies on-policy distillation to multi-agent routing cost

open_questions: Does the advantage-based method beat plain on-policy distillation on agentic coding tasks, not only its own benchmarks?
Does any group release code that reproduces the OPRD long-horizon results?
Do EvoRouter's cost savings hold on production query mixes outside its own benchmark?
